9	/-!
10	# The Abel map at the empty divisor
11	
12	`Picard/DivFamilyZero.lean` supplies the first inhabitant of `Scheme.DivFamily`. This
13	file spends it on the one place where having an inhabitant changes what can be
14	*checked* rather than merely stated: the **Abel map**
15	
16	  `A_{C/k} : Div_{C/k} ⟶ Pic^♯_{C/k}`,  `[D] ↦ [O(D)] = -[I_D]`.
17	
18	`Scheme.PicScheme.abelMap_app_mk` (`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`) states the
19	defining property `A([D]) = -[ker q]` for an arbitrary family. Before this file that
20	equation had **no instantiation**: `DivFamily` had no producer, so no value of the Abel
21	map was ever computed, and "the Abel map sends divisors to their line bundles" was a
22	statement about an empty domain.
23	
24	## What is proved
25	
26	`abelMap_zero`: `A([∅]) = 0`, i.e. the empty divisor goes to the **identity** of the
27	relative Picard group. Kleiman §3: `O(∅) = O`, so this is the normalisation an Abel map
28	must satisfy, and it is the first computed value of `abelMap` in the project.
29	
30	The proof is where the empty divisor's arithmetic shows up. `ker (0 : O_{X_T} ⟶ 0)` is
31	`O_{X_T}` (`Limits.kernelZeroIsoSource`, composed with
32	`Scheme.Modules.pullbackUnitIso` because `DivFamily.q`'s source is stated as the
33	*pulled-back* unit). The zero of `PicSharp.relPresheaf` is *by definition* the class of
34	the unit line bundle (`Scheme.PicSharp.addCommGroup_via_tensorObj`), so the ideal class
35	is the group identity, and `neg_zero` finishes.
36	
37	## What this is not
38	
39	It is not a step of the seam: `Scheme.fgaPicardRepresentability` is untouched, and no
40	antecedent of it is witnessed. It also does **not** discharge
41	`IdentityComponent.ClassDegreePinned`'s acceptance test
42	(`classDegree_ne_zero_of_exists_pos_fiberDeg`), which needs a divisor family of
43	degree `d ≠ 0` — the empty divisor has degree `0`, so it is exactly the family that
44	test cannot use. That producer is still owed, and it needs a rational point.
45	
46	What it does buy: the Abel map's defining equation, and the degree ledger of
47	`Picard/DivDegree.lean`, now have a worked instance to be wrong about. `abelDeg_zero`
48	below records the same value through the degree-refined Abel map, which is the form the
49	campaign's D-cluster consumes.
50	-/

62	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
63	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
64	
65	/-- **The ideal sheaf of the empty divisor is the structure sheaf**, as a class in the
66	relative Picard group: `[I_∅] = [O] = 0`.
67	
68	`ker (0 : O_{X_T} ⟶ 0) ≅ O_{X_T}` by `kernelZeroIsoSource`, then
69	`Modules.pullbackUnitIso` identifies `DivFamily.q`'s pulled-back-unit source with the
70	structure sheaf, and the zero of `relPresheaf` *is* the unit class. -/
71	theorem PicSharp.kernelClass_divFamilyZero (T : (Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))ᵒᵖ) :
72	    (Quotient.mk (PicSharp.relPicSetoid C.hom T.unop.hom)
73	      (⟨kernel (DivFamily.zero C.hom T.unop).q,
74	        (DivFamily.zero C.hom T.unop).kerLocallyTrivial⟩ :
75	        LineBundle.OnProduct C.hom T.unop.hom))
76	      = (0 : (PicSharp.relPresheaf C).obj T) :=
77	  Quotient.sound (PicSharp.relPicRel_of_iso
78	    ⟨Limits.kernelZeroIsoSource ≪≫ Scheme.Modules.pullbackUnitIso _⟩)
79	
80	variable [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom]
81	
82	/-- **THE ABEL MAP SENDS THE EMPTY DIVISOR TO THE IDENTITY**: `A([∅]) = 0`.
83	
84	`O(∅) = O` (Kleiman §3), the normalisation any Abel map must satisfy — and the **first
85	computed value of `abelMap` in this project**, since `DivFamily` had no inhabitant to
86	evaluate it at before `Picard/DivFamilyZero.lean`.
87	
88	Stated against `abelMapWitness`'s instance, i.e. via `abelMap_app_mk`, not under an
89	arbitrary `[HasAbelMap C]` binder — that class is a data slot inhabited by the constant
90	zero map, for which `abelMap_app_mk` provably fails (see its docstring, `I-0953`). Under
91	*that* inhabitant this equation would hold trivially and say nothing, which is exactly
92	why the instance matters here. -/
93	theorem PicScheme.abelMap_zero (T : (Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))ᵒᵖ) :
94	    (PicScheme.abelMap C).app T
95	        (Quotient.mk (DivFamily.setoid C.hom T.unop) (DivFamily.zero C.hom T.unop))
96	      = (0 : (PicSharp.relPresheaf C).obj T) := by
97	  rw [PicScheme.abelMap_app_mk, PicSharp.kernelClass_divFamilyZero]
98	  exact neg_zero (G := ((PicSharp.relPresheaf C).obj T : Type _))
99	
100	/-- **The degree-refined Abel map at the empty divisor**, in the form the campaign's
101	D-cluster consumes: `A⁰([∅]) = 0`.
102	
103	`abelDeg C 0` is `divFunctorDegι ≫ abelMapWitness`, so this is `abelMap_zero` transported
104	along the degree-`0` inclusion; `abelDeg_app_mk` supplies the transport. -/
105	theorem PicScheme.abelDeg_zero (T : (Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))ᵒᵖ) :
106	    (PicScheme.abelDeg C 0).app T (DivFunctorDeg.zeroClass C.hom T.unop)
107	      = (0 : (PicSharp.relPresheaf C).obj T) := by
108	  rw [show (DivFunctorDeg.zeroClass C.hom T.unop) =
109	      ⟨Quotient.mk (DivFamily.setoid C.hom T.unop) (DivFamily.zero C.hom T.unop),
110	        DivFunctor.classHasFiberDeg_zeroClass C.hom T.unop⟩ from rfl,
111	    PicScheme.abelDeg_app_mk]
112	  exact PicScheme.abelMap_zero C T
113

8	/-!
9	# The empty divisor: the first inhabitant of `Scheme.DivFamily`
10	
11	`Scheme.DivFamily π T` (`Picard/DivFunctorDef.lean`) is the carrier of the whole
12	divisor side of the Milne–Kollár campaign: `Scheme.DivFunctor`, its degree slices
13	`Scheme.DivFunctorDeg`, the Abel maps `abelDeg` / `abelMapWitness`, the flatness
14	inputs of `Picard/DivPushforwardFlat.lean`, and `IdentityComponent`'s
15	`ClassDegreePinned` acceptance test are all quantified over it. Until this file it
16	had **zero producers**, for any `π`, any base, and any test object including the
17	trivial one — measured with `exact?` and recorded in its own docstring. The
18	consequence recorded there: *every* statement quantified over a `DivFamily` was
19	"true but untested", with no instance to be wrong about.
20	
21	This file supplies the first inhabitant, unconditionally in `π : X ⟶ S` and
22	`T : Over S`: the **empty divisor** `D = ∅`, whose structure sheaf `O_D` is the
23	zero module and whose ideal is all of `O_{X_T}`.
24	
25	## Why the empty divisor satisfies the divisor condition
26	
27	The divisor condition of `DivFamily` is that the kernel ideal `I = ker q` be
28	*invertible* (`LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial`). For `q : O_{X_T} ⟶ 0` the kernel is
29	`O_{X_T}` itself (`Limits.kernelZeroIsoSource`), and the structure sheaf is
30	trivially locally trivial (`Scheme.PicSharp.isLocallyTrivial_unit`, restated here as
31	`isLocallyTrivial_unit'` because that one is `private`). So the invertible-ideal
32	condition — the field that makes `DivFamily` a divisor rather than an arbitrary
33	quotient — holds *for the reason it should*: `O_{X_T}/O_{X_T} = 0` cuts out the
34	empty subscheme, an effective divisor of degree zero.
35	
36	The three remaining fields are properties of the zero module, and the file proves
37	each rather than assuming it:
38	
39	* `isFinitePresentation` — the zero module is finitely presented. Mathlib has no
40	  instance for this (measured: `infer_instance` and `exact?` both fail on
41	  `(0 : Y.Modules).IsFinitePresentation`), so §1 builds the `QuasicoherentData`:
42	  the singleton family `{⊤}` covers the top of the opens site
43	  (`coversTop_singleton_top`), the restriction functor preserves zero objects
44	  (`preservesZeroMorphisms_overFunctor`, proved from `PresheafOfModules` extensionality
45	  because instance search for it times out), and a zero sheaf of modules has an
46	  *empty* presentation — no generators and no relations, both trivially finite.
47	* `flat` — flatness over the base. The section modules of a zero module are
48	  subsingletons, and a subsingleton module is flat.
49	* `properSupport` — the schematic support of the zero module is the subscheme cut
50	  out by the annihilator, which is `⊤`, so the support is **empty**
51	  (`Scheme.IdealSheafData.instIsEmptyCarrierCarrierCommRingCatSubschemeTop`) and any
52	  morphism out of it is proper via `IsProper.instOfIsFinite`. It is free here for that
53	  reason, and in particular with **no properness assumption on `π`**. (An earlier
54	  revision added "and it is a real hypothesis for a nonempty divisor". That half was
55	  never measured — nothing here or elsewhere in the project exhibits a divisor where
56	  `properSupport` fails or is expensive, and `DivFunctorDef.lean` says it is *automatic*
57	  when `π` is proper. Dropped rather than repaired: the free-here half is what this
58	  file establishes.)
59	
60	## What this does and does not buy
61	
62	**Does**: the divisor cluster is no longer vacuous. `Nonempty (DivFamily π T)` for
63	every `π` and `T`; `(DivFunctor π).obj (op T)` and `(DivFunctorDeg π 0).obj (op T)`
64	are inhabited; `HasFiberDeg zero 0`; and the base-change action carries `zero` to
65	`zero` (`pullbackAlong_zero`), so the classes are a global section of `DivFunctor`
66	rather than a fibrewise accident. Every theorem in `DivDegree.lean` and
67	`DivPushforwardFlat.lean` now has a witness to be checked against.
68	
69	**Does not**: this closes no `sorry` and witnesses no antecedent of
70	`Scheme.fgaPicardRepresentability`. In particular it is *not* a step of D1′: the
71	campaign's D1′ wants divisor families of a **prescribed positive degree** `d`
72	arising from a very ample `O(1)`, which needs the projectivity input
73	(`AJC.picrep.projectivity`) and P5 uniform `H¹` vanishing. What the empty divisor
74	does for that programme is remove the possibility that the target type is
75	uninhabited — a question that had to be settled before any positive-degree producer
76	could be believed, and which no lane had settled in either direction.
77	
78	**One caveat, stated because it is the natural over-reading.** The degree-zero slice
79	being inhabited does *not* make `DivFunctorDeg π 0` representable by the terminal
80	object `Over.mk (𝟙 S)`. That would need the slice to be a *singleton* at every test
81	object, and this file proves only the `Nonempty` half. The missing half is
82	`Subsingleton ((DivFunctorDeg π 0).obj (op T))` — i.e. that the empty divisor is the
83	*only* relative divisor of degree `0`. That is the expected statement (a degree-`0`
84	effective divisor on a fibre of a relative curve is empty), but it is a fact about
85	`fiberDeg`, not a formality: `fiberDeg` is a `finrank` with a junk value at
86	infinite dimension. Neither direction is proved here.
87	
88	**Corrected, and the correction is the useful part** (fresh-context audit of this file,
89	2026-07-30). An earlier revision of this paragraph said "no lane holds it". That is
90	FALSE: the analogous `Subsingleton` *is* landed, hours earlier, on the **sibling**
91	project's carrier — `instSubsingletonDivFamZarZero`
92	(`AJCR Picard/DivisorFamilyDegreeZeroUnique.lean`) and, over an arbitrary test ring,
93	`instSubsingletonDivFamZarZeroGeneral` plus a full `RepresentableBy` producer
94	(`AJCR Picard/DivisorFamilyDegreeZeroRep.lean`).
95	
96	What survives, for a **sharper** reason than the carrier mismatch: their proof is not
97	portable because it never passes through a `finrank` at all. It runs on `IsCertified`
98	and `rankAtStalk_eq_zero_iff_subsingleton` over `Away` localisations of section rings,
99	machinery that exists only on the Zariski-certified carrier `DivFamZar : Type u`. AJC's
100	`fiberDeg` is a `Module.finrank` of fibre sections. So the honest statement is: nobody
101	holds it *for `Scheme.DivFamily`*, and the sibling's landed route does not transport.
102	Their success is also evidence *against* this paragraph's own framing — it shows
103	degree-zero uniqueness can be reached without any finiteness-of-sections argument on a
104	suitable carrier, so "needs finiteness of the fibre sections" is a claim about AJC's
105	chosen `fiberDeg`, not about the mathematics. The row `AJC.picrep.divzero` records it as
106	the open question this file leaves.
107	
108	## Main declarations
109	
110	* `Scheme.DivFamily.zero π T` — the empty divisor family.
111	* `Scheme.DivFamily.instNonempty` — `Nonempty (DivFamily π T)`, as an instance.
112	* `Scheme.DivFamily.pullbackAlong_zero` — base change carries `zero` to `zero`.
113	* `Scheme.DivFamily.fiberDeg_zero` / `hasFiberDeg_zero` — the empty divisor has
114	  fibre degree `0` at every point.
115	* `Scheme.DivFunctor.zeroClass` / `Scheme.DivFunctorDeg.zeroClass` — the resulting
116	  inhabitants of the functor and of its degree-`0` slice, with
117	  `Scheme.DivFunctor.map_zeroClass` making the first a global section.
118	* `Scheme.Modules.isFinitePresentation_of_isZero` — reusable: a zero sheaf of
119	  modules on any scheme is finitely presented. Absent from Mathlib.
120	* `Scheme.Modules.coversTop_singleton_top`,
121	  `Scheme.Modules.preservesZeroMorphisms_overFunctor`,
122	  `Scheme.Modules.isZero_free_pempty` — the other reusable bricks §1 needed.
123	
124	Every declaration here is `sorry`-free and axiom-clean
125	(`[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`), measured against
126	`Scheme.fgaPicardRepresentability` reporting `sorryAx` in the same probe file with the
127	oleans rebuilt first.
128	
129	Reference: Kleiman, "The Picard scheme", §3 Def. `df:red`/`df:div`, Ex. `ex:DivC`
130	(arXiv:math/0504020).
131	-/

141	/-! ## §1. A zero sheaf of modules is finitely presented
142	
143	Mathlib carries no instance for this (`infer_instance` and `exact?` both fail on
144	`(0 : Y.Modules).IsFinitePresentation`), so the `QuasicoherentData` is built by
145	hand: one cover member `⊤`, no generators, no relations. -/
146	
147	namespace Scheme.Modules
148	
149	variable {Y : Scheme.{u}}
150	
151	/-- **The singleton family `{⊤}` covers the top of the opens site.**
152	
153	The one covering datum every "global" presentation needs, and the reason a *global*
154	presentation of a sheaf of modules on `Y` is already a `QuasicoherentData`: the sieve
155	`Sieve.ofObjects (fun _ => ⊤) V` is the top sieve at every open `V`, because
156	`V ≤ ⊤` supplies the required arrow. -/
157	theorem coversTop_singleton_top :
158	    (Opens.grothendieckTopology (Y : TopCat)).CoversTop
159	      (fun _ : PUnit.{u+1} => (⊤ : TopologicalSpace.Opens (Y : TopCat))) := by
160	  intro V
161	  have h : Sieve.ofObjects
162	      (fun _ : PUnit.{u+1} => (⊤ : TopologicalSpace.Opens (Y : TopCat))) V = ⊤ := by
163	    ext W _
164	    simp only [Sieve.top_apply, iff_true]
165	    exact ⟨PUnit.unit, ⟨homOfLE le_top⟩⟩
166	  rw [h]
167	  exact GrothendieckTopology.top_mem _ _
168	
169	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 1600000 in -- slice-site sheafification blow-up
170	set_option maxHeartbeats 2000000 in
171	/-- **The restriction functor to an open preserves zero morphisms.**
172	
173	`SheafOfModules.overFunctor` is `SheafOfModules.pushforward (𝟙 _)`, which acts as the
174	identity on section groups, so the statement is `rfl` componentwise. It is proved
175	rather than synthesized because instance search for
176	`(overFunctor Y.ringCatSheaf U).PreservesZeroMorphisms` exhausts its heartbeat budget
177	(measured: `deterministic timeout at typeclass, 20000 heartbeats`) — the
178	sheafification/slice-site instances it unfolds are the same blow-up
179	`Scheme.Modules.presentationPullbackιOfQuasicoherentData` documents. -/
180	theorem preservesZeroMorphisms_overFunctor (U : TopologicalSpace.Opens (Y : TopCat)) :
181	    (SheafOfModules.overFunctor Y.ringCatSheaf U).PreservesZeroMorphisms := by
182	  constructor
183	  intro _ _
184	  apply SheafOfModules.hom_ext
185	  apply PresheafOfModules.hom_ext
186	  intro _
187	  rfl
188	
189	/-- **The empty generating sections of a zero sheaf of modules.**
190	
191	No generators at all: the structure map `free PEmpty ⟶ M` is epi because *every*
192	morphism into a zero object is, so there is nothing to generate. Stated for a general
193	sheaf of rings on the opens site so that both `M` and its restrictions `M.over U`
194	can use it. -/
195	def zeroGeneratingSections
196	    {C : Type u} [Category.{u} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
197	    {R : Sheaf J RingCat.{u}} [HasWeakSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
198	    [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
199	    [J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ RingCat.{u} AddCommGrpCat.{u})]
200	    {M : SheafOfModules.{u} R} (hM : IsZero M) : M.GeneratingSections where
201	  I := PEmpty.{u+1}
202	  s j := PEmpty.elim j
203	  epi := ⟨fun {_} g h _ => hM.eq_of_src g h⟩
204	
205	instance zeroGeneratingSections_isFiniteType
206	    {C : Type u} [Category.{u} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
207	    {R : Sheaf J RingCat.{u}} [HasWeakSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
208	    [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
209	    [J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ RingCat.{u} AddCommGrpCat.{u})]
210	    {M : SheafOfModules.{u} R} (hM : IsZero M) :
211	    (zeroGeneratingSections hM).IsFiniteType where
212	  finite := (inferInstance : Finite PEmpty.{u+1})
213	
214	/-- **`free PEmpty` is an initial, hence zero, sheaf of modules.**
215	
216	There is exactly one morphism out of it into any target — `freeHomEquiv` turns a
217	morphism `free PEmpty ⟶ Z` into a family of sections indexed by `PEmpty`, of which
218	there is one — so it is initial, and an initial object in a category with zero
219	morphisms is a zero object. -/
220	theorem isZero_free_pempty
221	    {C : Type u} [Category.{u} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
222	    {R : Sheaf J RingCat.{u}} [HasWeakSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
223	    [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
224	    [J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ RingCat.{u} AddCommGrpCat.{u})] :
225	    IsZero (SheafOfModules.free (R := R) PEmpty.{u+1}) :=
226	  IsInitial.isZero <|
227	    IsInitial.ofUnique (h := fun Z =>
228	      ⟨⟨(SheafOfModules.freeHomEquiv Z).symm (fun j => PEmpty.elim j)⟩,
229	        fun _ => (SheafOfModules.freeHomEquiv Z).injective (funext fun j => PEmpty.elim j)⟩)
230	
231	/-- **A zero sheaf of modules has an empty presentation** — no generators and no
232	relations.
233	
234	The relations live in `kernel (zeroGeneratingSections hM).π`, whose source
235	`free PEmpty` is itself a zero object (`isZero_free_pempty`), so the kernel is zero
236	too and the empty family generates it for the same reason. -/
237	theorem isZero_kernel_zeroGeneratingSections
238	    {C : Type u} [Category.{u} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
239	    {R : Sheaf J RingCat.{u}} [HasWeakSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
240	    [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
241	    [J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ RingCat.{u} AddCommGrpCat.{u})]
242	    {M : SheafOfModules.{u} R} (hM : IsZero M) :
243	    IsZero (kernel (zeroGeneratingSections hM).π) :=
244	  haveI : Mono (zeroGeneratingSections hM).π := isZero_free_pempty.mono _
245	  isZero_kernel_of_mono _
246	
247	noncomputable def zeroPresentation
248	    {C : Type u} [Category.{u} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
249	    {R : Sheaf J RingCat.{u}} [HasWeakSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
250	    [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
251	    [J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ RingCat.{u} AddCommGrpCat.{u})]
252	    {M : SheafOfModules.{u} R} (hM : IsZero M) : M.Presentation where
253	  generators := zeroGeneratingSections hM
254	  relations := zeroGeneratingSections (isZero_kernel_zeroGeneratingSections hM)

257	    {C : Type u} [Category.{u} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
258	    {R : Sheaf J RingCat.{u}} [HasWeakSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
259	    [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
260	    [J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ RingCat.{u} AddCommGrpCat.{u})]
261	    {M : SheafOfModules.{u} R} (hM : IsZero M) : (zeroPresentation hM).IsFinite where
262	  isFiniteType_generators := zeroGeneratingSections_isFiniteType hM
263	  isFiniteType_relations :=
264	    zeroGeneratingSections_isFiniteType (isZero_kernel_zeroGeneratingSections hM)

268	/-- **The quasi-coherence datum of a zero sheaf of modules**: the singleton cover
269	`{⊤}`, with the empty presentation on it.
270	
271	The restriction `M.over ⊤` of a zero module is zero
272	(`preservesZeroMorphisms_overFunctor` plus `Functor.map_isZero`), so
273	`zeroPresentation` applies on the cover member. -/
274	theorem isZero_over_of_isZero {M : Y.Modules} (hM : IsZero M)
275	    (U : TopologicalSpace.Opens (Y : TopCat)) : IsZero (M.over U) :=
276	  haveI := preservesZeroMorphisms_overFunctor (Y := Y) U
277	  Functor.map_isZero (SheafOfModules.overFunctor Y.ringCatSheaf U) hM
278	
279	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 1600000 in -- slice-site `Over top` instances
280	set_option maxHeartbeats 2000000 in
281	noncomputable def zeroQuasicoherentData {M : Y.Modules} (hM : IsZero M) :
282	    M.QuasicoherentData where
283	  I := PUnit.{u+1}
284	  X _ := (⊤ : TopologicalSpace.Opens (Y : TopCat))
285	  coversTop := coversTop_singleton_top
286	  presentation _ := zeroPresentation (isZero_over_of_isZero hM _)
287	
288	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 1600000 in -- as `zeroQuasicoherentData` above
289	set_option maxHeartbeats 2000000 in
290	instance zeroQuasicoherentData_isFinitePresentation {M : Y.Modules} (hM : IsZero M) :
291	    (zeroQuasicoherentData hM).IsFinitePresentation where
292	  isFinite_presentation _ := zeroPresentation_isFinite (isZero_over_of_isZero hM _)
293	
294	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 1600000 in -- `shrink` re-enters slice synthesis
295	set_option maxHeartbeats 2000000 in
296	/-- **A zero sheaf of modules on a scheme is finitely presented.**
297	
298	Absent from Mathlib: measured, `infer_instance` and `exact?` both fail on
299	`(0 : Y.Modules).IsFinitePresentation`. This is the field of `Scheme.DivFamily` that
300	had no route at `F = 0`, and it is why the empty divisor needed §1 rather than one
301	line. Everything else about the empty divisor is a one-lemma citation. -/
302	theorem isFinitePresentation_of_isZero {M : Y.Modules} (hM : IsZero M) :
303	    M.IsFinitePresentation where
304	  exists_quasicoherentData :=
305	    ⟨(zeroQuasicoherentData hM).shrink,
306	      { isFinite_presentation := fun _ =>
307	          zeroPresentation_isFinite (isZero_over_of_isZero hM _) }⟩
308	
309	/-! ## §2. Flatness and proper support of a zero sheaf of modules -/
310	
311	/-- **The sections of a zero sheaf of modules over any open form a subsingleton.**
312	
313	`Scheme.Modules.toPresheaf` is additive, so it carries `M` to a zero presheaf of
314	abelian groups, whose value at `V` is a zero object of `Ab` and hence a
315	subsingleton. -/
316	theorem subsingleton_sections_of_isZero {M : Y.Modules} (hM : IsZero M)
317	    (V : Y.Opens) : Subsingleton Γ(M, V) :=
318	  AddCommGrpCat.subsingleton_of_isZero
319	    ((Functor.map_isZero (Scheme.Modules.toPresheaf Y) hM).obj _)
320	
321	/-- **A zero sheaf of modules is flat over any base morphism**, with no hypothesis on
322	the morphism at all.
323	
324	`CoherentSheafFlat` asks each section module `Γ(M, V)` to be flat over `Γ(S, U)`. The
325	section modules are subsingletons (`subsingleton_sections_of_isZero`), and a
326	subsingleton module is flat. -/
327	theorem coherentSheafFlat_of_isZero {S' : Scheme.{u}} (g : Y ⟶ S') {M : Y.Modules}
328	    (hM : IsZero M) : Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat g M := by
329	  intro U _ V _ e
330	  letI : Module Γ(S', U) Γ(M, V) := Module.compHom _ (g.appLE U V e).hom
331	  haveI := subsingleton_sections_of_isZero hM V
332	  exact inferInstance
333	
334	/-- **The annihilator ideal sheaf of a zero sheaf of modules is `⊤`.**
335	
336	Each affine-local annihilator is the whole ring (`Module.annihilator_eq_top_iff` at a
337	subsingleton module), and `ofIdeals` of the constant-`⊤` family is `⊤` because `⊤` is
338	itself an ideal sheaf below it. -/
339	theorem annihilator_of_isZero {M : Y.Modules} (hM : IsZero M) :
340	    Scheme.Modules.annihilator M = ⊤ :=
341	  top_le_iff.mp (le_sSup (by
342	    intro U
343	    haveI := subsingleton_sections_of_isZero hM U.1
344	    exact le_of_eq (Module.annihilator_eq_top_iff.mpr inferInstance).symm))
345	
346	/-- **The schematic support of a zero sheaf of modules is empty.**
347	
348	Its annihilator is `⊤`, and the subscheme cut out by the unit ideal sheaf has empty
349	carrier. -/
350	theorem isEmpty_schematicSupport_of_isZero {M : Y.Modules} (hM : IsZero M) :
351	    IsEmpty (Scheme.Modules.schematicSupport M) := by
352	  rw [Scheme.Modules.schematicSupport, annihilator_of_isZero hM]
353	  infer_instance
354	
355	/-- **A zero sheaf of modules has proper support over any base**, unconditionally.
356	
357	The support is empty, and a morphism out of an empty scheme is finite, hence proper.
358	This is the field of `DivFamily` that is a *real* hypothesis for a nonempty divisor —
359	properness of `D → T` — and it is free for the empty one, with **no** properness
360	assumption on the ambient morphism. -/
361	theorem hasProperSupport_of_isZero {S' : Scheme.{u}} (g : Y ⟶ S') {M : Y.Modules}
362	    (hM : IsZero M) : Scheme.Modules.HasProperSupport g M := by
363	  haveI := isEmpty_schematicSupport_of_isZero hM
364	  exact IsProper.instOfIsFinite _
365	
366	end Scheme.Modules
367	
368	/-! ## §3. The empty divisor -/
369	
370	namespace Scheme
371	
372	variable {S X : Scheme.{u}} (π : X ⟶ S) (T : Over S)
373	
374	/-- **The structure sheaf is locally trivial of rank one.**
375	
376	`Scheme.PicSharp.isLocallyTrivial_unit` is `private`, so it is restated here rather
377	than reused: on any affine open the identity is the required trivialisation. -/
378	theorem isLocallyTrivial_unit' {Y : Scheme.{u}} :
379	    LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial (SheafOfModules.unit Y.ringCatSheaf) := by
380	  intro x
381	  obtain ⟨W, hW_aff, hxW, -⟩ :=
382	    exists_isAffineOpen_mem_and_subset (X := Y) (x := x) (U := ⊤)
383	      (show x ∈ (⊤ : Y.Opens) from trivial)
384	  exact ⟨W, hxW, hW_aff,
385	    ⟨(Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctorIsoPullback W.ι).app _ ≪≫ Modules.pullbackUnitIso W.ι⟩⟩
386	
387	/-- **THE EMPTY DIVISOR**, and with it the first inhabitant of `Scheme.DivFamily` for
388	any `π : X ⟶ S` and any test object `T`.
389	
390	`F = 0`, `q = 0`. The kernel ideal is then all of `O_{X_T}` — via
391	`Limits.kernelZeroIsoSource`, since the source of `q` is the pulled-back unit — which
392	is invertible, so the *divisor condition* holds for the geometric reason it should:
393	`O_{X_T}/O_{X_T} = 0` cuts out `D = ∅`, an effective relative divisor.
394	
395	No hypothesis on `π`: not proper, not smooth, not even separated. Compare the general
396	case, where `properSupport` and `flat` are substantive conditions. -/
397	noncomputable def DivFamily.zero : DivFamily π T where
398	  F := 0
399	  isFinitePresentation := Modules.isFinitePresentation_of_isZero (isZero_zero _)
400	  flat := Modules.coherentSheafFlat_of_isZero _ (isZero_zero _)
401	  properSupport := Modules.hasProperSupport_of_isZero _ (isZero_zero _)
402	  q := 0
403	  epi := (isZero_zero _).epi _
404	  kerLocallyTrivial :=
405	    LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial.of_iso
406	      (Limits.kernelZeroIsoSource (X := (Scheme.Modules.pullback
407	        (Limits.pullback.fst π T.hom)).obj (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf))
408	        (Y := (0 : (Limits.pullback π T.hom).Modules))).symm
409	      (LineBundle.IsLocallyTrivial.of_iso
410	        (Modules.pullbackUnitIso (Limits.pullback.fst π T.hom)).symm
411	        isLocallyTrivial_unit')
412	
413	instance DivFamily.instNonempty : Nonempty (DivFamily π T) :=
414	  ⟨DivFamily.zero π T⟩
415	
416	/-! ## §4. Base change, fibre degree, and the degree-zero slice
417	
418	The empty divisor is not just a fibrewise accident: base change carries it to the
419	empty divisor of the new test object, so its classes assemble into a **global section**
420	of `DivFunctor`, and its fibre degree is `0` at every point of every base. -/
421	
422	/-- **The pulled-back empty divisor is the empty divisor**, up to the divisor
423	equivalence — both `F`-sheaves are zero and any two morphisms into a zero object
424	agree.
425	
426	This is what makes `zeroClass` below a genuine global section of `DivFunctor` rather
427	than an unrelated choice at each test object. -/
428	theorem DivFamily.pullbackAlong_zero {T' : Over S} (ψ : T' ⟶ T) :
429	    ((DivFamily.zero π T).pullbackAlong ψ).Rel (DivFamily.zero π T') :=
430	  ⟨(Functor.map_isZero (Scheme.Modules.pullback (quotBaseMap π ψ))
431	      (isZero_zero _)).iso (isZero_zero _),
432	    (isZero_zero _).eq_of_tgt _ _⟩
433	
434	/-- **The fibre of the empty divisor is zero** — `fiberModule` is a module pullback,
435	which is additive. -/
436	theorem DivFamily.isZero_fiberModule_zero (t : (T.left : Scheme.{u})) :
437	    IsZero ((Limits.pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberModule t (DivFamily.zero π T).F) :=
438	  Functor.map_isZero _ (isZero_zero _)
439	
440	/-- **The empty divisor has fibre degree `0`**, at every point of every base.
441	
442	`deg ∅ = dim_{κ(t)} Γ(∅, O_∅) = 0`: the fibre is the zero module, its global sections
443	are a subsingleton, and `finrank` of a subsingleton is `0`. -/
444	theorem DivFamily.fiberDeg_zero (t : (T.left : Scheme.{u})) :
445	    (DivFamily.zero π T).fiberDeg t = 0 := by
446	  letI := (Limits.pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberSectionsModule t
447	    ((Limits.pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberModule t (DivFamily.zero π T).F)
448	  haveI : Subsingleton
449	      Γ((Limits.pullback.snd π T.hom).fiberModule t (DivFamily.zero π T).F, ⊤) :=
450	    Modules.subsingleton_sections_of_isZero (DivFamily.isZero_fiberModule_zero π T t) _
451	  exact Module.finrank_zero_of_subsingleton
452	
453	/-- **The empty divisor has constant fibre degree `0`** — `HasFiberDeg zero 0`, the
454	predicate the degree-`d` subfunctor `DivFunctorDeg` is cut out by. -/
455	theorem DivFamily.hasFiberDeg_zero : (DivFamily.zero π T).HasFiberDeg 0 :=
456	  fun t => DivFamily.fiberDeg_zero π T t
457	
458	/-- **The class of the empty divisor** in `Div_{X/S}(T)`: the first inhabitant of the
459	relative-divisor functor's value at any test object. -/
460	noncomputable def DivFunctor.zeroClass : (DivFunctor π).obj (Opposite.op T) :=
461	  Quotient.mk _ (DivFamily.zero π T)
462	
463	instance DivFunctor.instNonemptyObj : Nonempty ((DivFunctor π).obj (Opposite.op T)) :=
464	  ⟨DivFunctor.zeroClass π T⟩
465	
466	/-- **`DivFunctor` carries the zero class to the zero class**, i.e. `zeroClass` is a
467	*global section* of `Div_{X/S}` — a compatible family over all test objects, not a
468	choice per object. -/
469	theorem DivFunctor.map_zeroClass {T' : Over S} (ψ : T' ⟶ T) :
470	    (DivFunctor π).map ψ.op (DivFunctor.zeroClass π T) = DivFunctor.zeroClass π T' :=
471	  Quotient.sound (DivFamily.pullbackAlong_zero π T ψ)
472	
473	/-- **The empty divisor's class has degree `0`**, in the class-level predicate the
474	degree slices use. -/
475	theorem DivFunctor.classHasFiberDeg_zeroClass :
476	    DivFamily.ClassHasFiberDeg (π := π) 0 (DivFunctor.zeroClass π T) :=
477	  DivFamily.hasFiberDeg_zero π T
478	
479	/-- **The degree-`0` slice `Div⁰_{X/S}(T)` is inhabited**, for every `π` and every
480	test object.
481	
482	This is the statement that turns the whole degree apparatus of `Picard/DivDegree.lean`
483	from vacuous into tested. Note what it is *not*: an identification of the slice with a
484	point. See the file docstring — singleton-ness at every test object is what
485	representability by the terminal object would need, and that is open. -/
486	noncomputable def DivFunctorDeg.zeroClass : (DivFunctorDeg π 0).obj (Opposite.op T) :=
487	  ⟨DivFunctor.zeroClass π T, DivFunctor.classHasFiberDeg_zeroClass π T⟩
488	
489	instance DivFunctorDeg.instNonemptyObjZero :
490	    Nonempty ((DivFunctorDeg π 0).obj (Opposite.op T)) :=
491	  ⟨DivFunctorDeg.zeroClass π T⟩
492	
493	end Scheme
494	
495	end AlgebraicGeometry

11	/-!
12	# FGA representability of the Picard scheme
13	
14	This file states the FGA representability of the relative Picard functor of a
15	smooth proper geometrically integral curve `C/k`, following Kleiman, "The
16	Picard scheme", §2 and §4 (cf. FGA Explained Ch. 9; arXiv:math/0504020).
17	
18	The relative Picard functor is
19	
20	```
21	picSharp C := PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⋙ forget AddCommGrpCat
22	```
23	
24	the set-valued shadow of the `H_T`-coset carrier
25	`T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)` of `Picard/RelPicFunctor.lean` (Kleiman §2
26	Def. `df:Pfs`; blueprint `def:rel_pic_sharp`). A `RepresentableBy` witness
27	against it is a natural bijection
28	`(T ⟶ Pic_{C/k}) ≃ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)`, which is what the downstream
29	tangent-space computation (`AJC.pic0av`, `Pic0.tangentSpaceIso`) attaches to.
30	
31	## The étale-sheafification route (owner decision of 2026-07-28)
32	
33	Kleiman §4 represents the **étale-sheafified** functor `Pic_{(C/k)ét}`, and
34	that is what this file's obligation is stated against —
35	`fgaPicardRepresentability`, over an **arbitrary** base field, with **no
36	hypothesis on `C(k)`**. The functor is built and its sheaf property proved in
37	`Picard/PicEtSheaf.lean` (`PicScheme.picEt`, `picEt_isSheaf_forget`), by
38	sheafifying the relative Picard presheaf for Mathlib's big étale topology
39	localised at `Spec k`.
40	
41	Why the sheafification is not optional. The plain relative functor
42	`picSharp C = T ↦ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)` is not representable over a
43	general field, so an unconditional `RepresentableBy` against `picSharp` is a
44	**false** statement, not merely an unproved one.
45	
46	**CITATION CORRECTED 2026-07-29 (`review-ajc`), by reading the source. The
47	conclusion above is right; the reason previously given for it was not.** This
48	paragraph used to say `picSharp` "is not even a Zariski sheaf (Kleiman §2
49	L1292–L1302)". Those lines
50	(`references/kleiman-picard-src/kleiman-picard.tex`, the full paper) say
51	something else: "The **absolute** Picard functor `Pic_X` is never a separated
52	presheaf in the Zariski topology", proved with the `ℙ¹_X`/`O(1)` argument. That
53	is about `Pic_X`, **not** about the relative `Pic_{X/S} = picSharp`, which is
54	*defined* by quotienting out `Pic(T)` precisely to defeat that argument. What
55	Kleiman actually asserts about the relative functor is weaker (L1330): "Since
56	`Pic_{X/S}` is not *a priori* a sheaf, it is remarkable that it is representable
57	so often in practice." Not-a-priori is not never — indeed L1600–L1605 proves
58	`Pic_{X/S} ≅ Pic_{(X/S)zar}` whenever `f` has a section.
59	
60	**The witness, and it satisfies exactly this file's binders.** Kleiman
61	L5105–L5108 (repeated L5126–L5129): take `X : u² + v² + w² = 0` in `ℙ²_ℝ`, a
62	smooth plane conic — hence smooth, proper, and geometrically integral, since
63	`X_ℂ ≅ ℙ¹_ℂ` — over a field where it has **no** rational point. `Pic_{(X/ℝ)ét}`
64	is representable by §4 `th:main`, the two functors differ (Exercise `ex:Pfs`),
65	and Kleiman concludes `Pic_{X/ℝ}` is not representable.
66	
67	**That last step is now a Lean theorem rather than a quotation**, which is the
68	right state for something this load-bearing:
69	`PicScheme.not_exists_representing_picSharp_of_not_isIso`
70	(`Picard/PicEtSubcanonical.lean`, `ajc-p1`) derives *from* `¬ IsIso
71	(picEtComparison C)` that **no** scheme represents `picSharp C` — the existential
72	of clause (1), not merely the pinned `PicScheme C`. No topology and no sheaf step
73	enter. So the falsity of the `picSharp` analogue of clause (1) is reduced to the
74	single residue that the comparison really does fail for that conic (via
75	`φ^* O(1)` and `h⁰` on `ℙ¹_ℂ`), which is where Kleiman's own argument lives and
76	is not yet formalised.
77	
78	**Do not route this through a Zariski-sheaf claim** (corrected again the same
79	day, after `work-reviewer` refuted the first repair — see `I-0970`). It is
80	tempting to argue "representable ⟹ Zariski sheaf, and `picSharp` is not one";
81	the second half is *not* what the sources say. `ex:Pfs` compares
82	`Pic_{(X/ℝ)zar}` with `Pic_{(X/ℝ)ét}` — both already sheaves — so it witnesses
83	`zar ≠ ét`, not a failure of Zariski descent for the unsheafified functor. And
84	Kleiman `th:cmp` part 1 (L1391–L1393) proves `Pic_{X/S} ↪ Pic_{(X/S)zar}`
85	whenever `O_S ≅ f_* O_X` holds universally, which is automatic on these binders —
86	i.e. `picSharp` *is* Zariski-separated here, and any failure could only be
87	gluing. The non-representability above needs no sheaf step at all, so take it
88	directly. Kleiman §2 **Thm 2.5** repairs it only under a
89	**section**: given one (and `O_S = f_* O_X` universally, automatic for our
90	proper geometrically integral `C/k`), the comparisons
91	
92	```
93	Pic_{X/S}(T) → Pic_{(X/S)ét}(T) → Pic_{(X/S)fppf}(T)
94	```
95	
96	are bijective. That conditional route survives here as
97	`picEtComparison_isIso_of_hasRationalPoint` and `picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint`,
98	both clearly labelled as **strictly weaker than the challenge**. They are not
99	the headline and must not be reported as progress toward it. (Earlier revisions
100	of this file named a class `PicEtComparisonIso` in these four places; no such
101	declaration exists or ever landed — the comparison is supplied by the theorem
102	`picEtComparison_isIso_of_hasRationalPoint`, which is clause (2) of
103	`fgaPicardRepresentability` applied to the section. Corrected 2026-07-29.)
104	
105	The two interfaces, and which one to build against:
106	
107	* `HasPicSchemeEt` / `PicSchemeEt` / `representableEt` / `groupSchemeStructureEt`
108	  — **unconditional**, the étale formulation, the target. New work goes here.
109	* `HasPicScheme` / `PicScheme` / `representable` / `groupSchemeStructure` — the
110	  legacy `picSharp`-shaped interface, whose only producer is now the
111	  conditional `picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint`. Consumers quantifying over
112	  `[HasPicScheme C]` as a hypothesis remain valid and kernel-clean; they are
113	  simply conditional statements until restated against `picEt`.
114	
115	## Main results
116	
117	* `fgaPicardRepresentability` — **the project's central open obligation**:
118	  representability of `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` over an arbitrary field, no rational
119	  point. The file's only `sorry`.
120	* `HasPicSchemeEt`, `PicSchemeEt`, `representableEt`,
121	  `instPicSchemeEtLocallyOfFiniteType`, `instPicSchemeEtIsSeparated`,
122	  `groupSchemeStructureEt` — the unconditional étale interface derived from it.
123	* `picEtComparison_isIso_of_hasRationalPoint`, `picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint` —
124	  the **conditional** Kleiman §2 Thm 2.5 route, strictly weaker than the
125	  challenge, not the headline.
126	* `picSharp` — the relative Picard functor `Pic^♯_{C/k}`.
127	* `divFunctor` — the relative-divisor functor `Scheme.DivFunctor C.hom` of
128	  `Picard/DivFunctorDef.lean` (Kleiman §3 Def. `df:div`, invertible-kernel
129	  quotient encoding).
130	* `PicScheme`, `representable`, `instPicSharpRepresentable` — the representing
131	  scheme and the natural bijection
132	  `(T ⟶ Pic_{C/k}) ≃ Pic(C ×_k T)/π_T^* Pic(T)` it induces.
133	* `instPicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType`, `isSeparated` — `Pic_{C/k}` is locally
134	  of finite type and separated over `k` (Kleiman §4 Thm `th:main`(1): it is a
135	  disjoint union of open quasi-projective `k`-subschemes).
136	* `groupSchemeStructure` — `Pic_{C/k}` is a commutative `k`-group scheme, by
137	  Yoneda transport (`CommGrpObj.ofRepresentableBy`) of the abelian-group
138	  structure of `PicSharp.relPresheaf`.
139	* `abelMapWitness`, `abelMap`, `abelMap_app_mk` — the Abel map
140	  `Div_{C/k} ⟶ Pic^♯_{C/k}`, `[D] ↦ [O(D)] = -[ker q]` (Kleiman §3
141	  Def. `dfn:Abel`), assembled as `abelKernelNatTrans C ≫ picNeg C`.
142	* `smoothProperQuotient` — the Altman–Kleiman quotient lemma (Kleiman §4
143	  Lem. `lm:qt`), relative to the use-site hypothesis class
144	  `HasSmoothProperQuotient`.
145	
146	## Remaining obligations
147	
148	**Exactly one** statement in this file is `sorry`: `fgaPicardRepresentability`,
149	the existence of a scheme representing the étale-sheafified relative Picard
150	functor `Pic_{(C/k)ét}` and separated and locally of finite type over `k`, for
151	an arbitrary field `k` and **no** hypothesis on `C(k)`. Mathematically this is
152	Kleiman §4 Thm `th:main`(1) together with Cor `cor:algsch`. It is the project's
153	central open obligation and is **expected to stay open**. Its inputs are the
154	Milne–Kollár ones — `Div^d` through the Grassmannian and a finite Galois
155	quotient — *not* Quot and *not* `smoothProperQuotient`; see the "Which route
156	discharges it" paragraph on `fgaPicardRepresentability` below, which corrects an
157	earlier claim here that the inputs were blocked on Quot. Everything else here —
158	the representing scheme,
159	its representability, local finiteness, separatedness and group-scheme
160	structure, and the conditional `picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint` — is derived from
161	that one existence statement.
162	
163	`smoothProperQuotient` is stated against an explicit hypothesis class rather
164	than proved outright, because the hypothesis list expressible here is weaker
165	than Kleiman §4 Lem. `lm:qt`: it omits quasi-projectivity of the representing
166	scheme `Y`, for which Mathlib has no vocabulary at the pinned revision.
167	Without that hypothesis the statement is false — a Hironaka-type free
168	`ℤ/2`-action on a smooth proper non-projective 3-fold gives a smooth proper
169	equivalence relation whose quotient étale sheaf is an algebraic space that is
170	not a scheme. The class must therefore be supplied at the use site, where
171	quasi-projectivity of the Abel-map slice is available.
172	
173	## References
174	
175	Blueprint: `blueprint/src/chapters/Picard_FGAPicRepresentability.tex`.
176	Kleiman, "The Picard scheme" (arXiv:math/0504020): §2 Thm 2.5
177	(`th:comp` comparison under a section), §3 Def `dfn:Abel` + Thm `th:repDiv`,
178	§4 Thm `th:main` + Cor `cor:algsch` + Lem `lm:qt`.
179	-/
180	
181	set_option autoImplicit false
182	
183	universe u
184	
185	open CategoryTheory Limits
186	
187	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
188	
189	namespace Scheme
190	
191	/-- **`C` has a `k`-rational point**: the structural morphism `C.hom` admits a
192	section `σ : Spec k ⟶ C.left`. For the smooth proper geometrically integral
193	curves of this project this is the pointing `P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec k)) ⟶ C`
194	already threaded through the Albanese statements (`AlgebraicJacobian.IsAlbanese`).
195	
196	This is the hypothesis of Kleiman §2 **Thm 2.5**: together with
